Definition: from G1537 and G1212; wholly evident:--manifest.
BiblicalUsage: This word means wholly evident, plain to everyone, and Paul uses it once, about the false teachers of the last days. Their folly shall be manifest to all men, as the folly of Jannes and Jambres was, and the exposure is certain even when the deception looks strong. The word promises that the truth will show.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe folly always shows itself in the end, because God does not let deception wear a disguise forever.
RelatedTopics: Truth; Judgment on false teachers; Judgment
